ir.name: loss_margin_rank_blend_tanh_weighted_advantage_gap_with_weight_norm
ir.intuition: Inject explicit normalization constraint by normalizing the instance weights so the total weight sums to one, ensuring the loss is scale-invariant with respect to weights. This stabilizes training by preventing weights from arbitrarily scaling the loss magnitude.
ir.pseudocode:
lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
adv_gap = batch['advantage_gap']
weight = batch.get('weight', ones_like(lpw))
weight_sum = sum(weight)
norm_weight = weight / max(weight_sum, epsilon)
margin = alpha * (lpw - lpl)
smooth_margin = tanh(clamp(margin, -10, 10))
weight_factor = abs(adv_gap)
hinge = relu(1 - smooth_margin)
loss = hinge * weight_factor * norm_weight
final_loss = mean(loss)
ir.code:
def generated_loss(batch, model_output, extra):
    lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
    lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
    adv_gap = batch['advantage_gap']
    weight = batch.get('weight', ops.ones_like(lpw))
    eps = 1e-12
    weight_sum = ops.sum(weight)
    norm_weight = ops.div(weight, ops.max(weight_sum, eps))
    alpha = float(extra.get('alpha', extra.get('hyperparams', {}).get('alpha', 1.0)))
    margin = ops.mul(alpha, ops.sub(lpw, lpl))
    clamped_margin = ops.clamp(margin, -10.0, 10.0)
    smooth_margin = ops.tanh(clamped_margin)
    weight_factor = ops.abs(adv_gap)
    hinge = ops.relu(ops.sub(ops.ones_like(smooth_margin), smooth_margin))
    loss = ops.mul(hinge, weight_factor)
    loss = ops.mul(loss, norm_weight)
    return ops.mean(loss)
